defect.description: The edge case where new_mobject is old_mobject: the new deduplication removes the object from the list before searching, so scene.replace(a, a) no longer finds a, raises ValueError and leaves a removed from the scene; the deduplication must skip the case new_m is old_m (or run only after the replacement).
defect.location: src/scene.py (the deduplication at the top of replace_in_list)

review_items: scene.py:37 — replace(x, x) raises ValueError because guard removes new_m before search
scene.py:37 — guard removes new_m from wrong nesting level in recursion
test_scene.py:29 — no test for replace(x, x)
test_scene.py:37 — no test for cross-level case
votes.evidence_quote: When `old_m is new_m`, the object is removed, then the loop can't find it, and `replace_in_list` returns `False`, causing `ValueError("Could not find …")` at line 52.
votes.justification: The review's first finding names the faulty behaviour: replace(x, x) raises ValueError. It also names the cause: the dedup guard removes new_m before the search, so the object is never found. It points at the right code in replace_in_list.
